newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Rosneft pulls out of Azeri oil deal - agency.
newsitem.headline: Russian Rosneft pulls out of Azeri oil deal - agency.

text.p: Russia's state-owned oil company Rosneft is pulling out of a $1 billion deal to develop a major Caspian oil deposit with LUKoil and Azeri state oil firm SOCAR, Interfax news agency said on Thursday.
The field, called Kyapaz by the Azeris, is at the centre of a territorial row between Turkmenistan and Azerbaijan.
Both say the field lies in their part of the Caspian, and Turkmen President Saparmurat Niyazov has complained to Russia over the Azeri-Rosneft-LUKoil agreement.

Interfax quoted Rosneft spokesman Vladimir Vyunitsky as saying Rosneft would continue to look at projects in the Caspian and had set up a working group to Azerbaijan and Turkmenistan to work on new deals.
It was not clear whether the new agreements might include the disputed field, which Turkmenistan calls Serdar. Vyunitsky, was not available for comment.

Rosneft signed the deal with LUKoil and SOCAR in July. Rosneft said it was a preliminary deal but said all sides were aware of conflicting territorial claims in the Caspian and did not expect them to affect the agreement.
The deposit contains estimated reserves of over 50 million tonnes.
SOCAR was to get a 50 percent share in the project, LUKoil 30 percent and Rosneft 20 percent.
Turkmenistan's Niyazov is due to visit Moscow next week, and the status of the Caspian is likely to be high on the agenda.

Oil companies involved in developing Caspian deposits have generally played down the likely impact of rowing littoral states. At stake are tens of billions of dollars worth of resources, in what analysts dub the world's last great oil game.
So far Azerbaijan and Kazakhstan have been most successful in attracting foreign investment, while Russia has operated mainly through its newly privatised companies.
